newsitem.title: UK: United News merger benefits to take time.
newsitem.headline: United News merger benefits to take time.

text.p: The real benefits of the merger between United News & Media and MAI Plc are not expected to feed through until next year, analysts said on Thursday.
They were commenting after the enlarged United News posted pre-tax pre-exceptional profits of 151.9 million stg for the six months to June 30, a rise of 21.5 percent.

Louise Barton of Henderson Crosthwaite said she was provisionally upgrading her forecast for 1997 pre-tax profit from 295 million stg to 320 million stg. "Essentially it's a management play with (chief executive Lord) Hollick moving and shaking a bit more aggressively than we thought," she said.
"It will take time to reorganise the whole thing but it should be starting to pay off by next year," she added.
Barton, who has a "buy" recommendation on United is forecasting a pre-tax pre-exceptional profit of around 290 million stg for 1996.
United shares added 6p to 711.5p on the results.

The two companies completed a merger in April to form a media major with market capitalisation of over three billion pounds and interests including national newspapers and ITV commercial television franchises.
Some analysts said that United had not painted a particularly clear picture of its performance in its presentation on Thursday.
"The top line seems fine but it's how they get to it that is confusing. We're a little in the dark about underlying trade," said one.
"There are huge exceptional items and I think the progress will come next year but the jury is still out," he added.
"They're spending a 100 million pounds to reshape the business and it will be a long payback," he said.

Another analyst, Anthony de Larrinaga of Panmure Gordon, retained his "hold" stance on United and said he had seen nothing to make him alter his 1996 pre-exceptional profit forecast of 292 million stg.
He predicts the figure will be around 175 million stg when all the exceptional costs are included.

De Larrinaga lamented the fact that United had not broken down the results from its Consumer Publishing to show how components such as Express Newspapers and United Provincial Newspapers were performing.
"I think United is fairly valued at current levels unless Hollick can pull a rabbit out of the hat on refocusing the businesses," he said.
